subject: Novamed: no-train commitment, SOW language, and KMS residency questions
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@novamed.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>, Rachel Conklin <rachel.conklin@deltapartners.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Question: no-train guarantee + SOW language and key residency

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — NovaMed is excited about Redwood's throughput profile. Before Procurement can clear the PO, Legal and Security have a few open asks around data use and DPA wording that I wanted to put to you directly: 

1) No-training / model improvement: can Redwood commit that data (prompts + generated responses) will not be used to improve models, either internally or via subprocessors? If not, what opt-out or contractual language do you offer? We need explicit SOW/DPA text we can show Legal.

2) Prompt/response ownership: we need confirmation that NovaMed retains all rights to prompts and outputs, and that Redwood will not assert derivative rights. Exact phrasing would help.

3) Key management & residency: our security team requires KMS keys to be resident in the EU for EU-submitted requests. Can you confirm KMS options and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) in EU regions?

4) Subprocessors and evidence: please provide the current subprocessor list and the operational evidence pack (runbooks or proof points) you provide to customers requesting a no-train commitment.

We'd like initial answers and proposed contract language by COB Monday so Procurement can include them in the SOW.

Best,
Elena
Elena Mendez
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | NovaMed

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@novamed.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>, Rachel Conklin <rachel.conklin@deltapartners.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: no-train guarantee + SOW language and key residency

Hi Elena — great question set, thank you. Quick ack — I copied our privacy lead (David) and product/security (Jordan) to provide the technical and contractual detail. 

High level answers up front:
- Redwood can offer a contractual no-training commitment for NovaMed data for this engagement. There are operational paths for evidence and onshore routing.
- We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and can route EU traffic to EU-resident KMS/HSM options for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers can request EU key residency for an enterprise setup.
- Subprocessor list attached and we can assemble an evidence pack that maps to the DPA clauses you need.

Attached: SOW_no-training_draft.docx (sample SOW clause + operational appendix).

Next step: David will propose exact DPA/SOW wording and the evidence scope. Can we schedule a 30-min call Monday (Jul 13) at 10am CET to review?

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0126

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: FW: NovaMed - no-train + SOW ask

FW: Elena's request above. Procurement needs concrete wording and timeline (COB Monday). Key asks: no-train commitment, explicit prompt/response ownership, EU KMS residency/BYOK options, subprocessor evidence.

My notes:
- Customer is launching a pilot across EU sites — EU residency is mandatory per their security lead.
- They'll accept a contractual no-train guarantee plus an evidence pack that shows subprocessor handling and routing.
- If we can't meet hosted KMS in EU immediately, they are open to Dedicated or Private deployment options for the pilot, but Procurement wants pricing and timeline.

Can you:
1) Suggest precise DPA/SOW text for the no-training clause and ownership language (David)
2) Confirm BYOK/KMS routing options and realistic cutover timeline for a Dedicated slot (Jordan)
3) Flag any subprocessors that could be blockers (Karthik)

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
-Markus

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@novamed.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: no-train commitment, SOW language, and KMS residency questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below is proposed language and the operational notes you requested. I focused on minimal, auditable commitments so Legal has something to review.

Proposed DPA/SOW wording (suggested insertion):
"No-Training Commitment: For the duration of the Agreement, Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Data (defined as prompts, user-provided documents, attachments, and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models, whether owned by Redwood or its subprocessors. Redwood shall process Customer Data only for the purpose of providing the Services described in the Agreement and shall not incorporate Customer Data into model training corpora.

Prompt/Output Ownership: Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data and any outputs generated by the Services. Redwood disclaims any ownership or derivative rights in such Customer Data and outputs."

Operational evidence and controls we will provide: 
- Subprocessor inventory (attached: subprocessors_list_202607.pdf). We will redact internal IPs but include vendor names, jurisdictions, and the role each plays.
- Evidence pack (guidance attached: evidence_pack_instructions.pdf) that includes: architecture diagram showing EU routing, KV/prefix caching policies, subprocessor dataflow maps, and a signed attestation from our Security team describing non-training handling.
- KMS/BYOK options: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS in EU regions. For Hosted customers we offer a managed EU-residency option for keys on enterprise plans; timeline to enable BYOK for a new Dedicated pool is typically 3–6 weeks depending on procurement and capacity.

Exceptions & practical notes:
- Very small operational telemetry (aggregated non-identifying metrics used for platform health) is collected — we will ensure these metrics are scrubbed of Customer Data and excluded from model training. We can add an explicit carve-out line to the DPA if helpful.
- If NovaMed requires evidence of no access by any subprocessors, we can negotiate an addendum committing that Redwood will not transfer Customer Data to certain third-party vendors (we have precedents for gating particular subprocessors).

Attachments: SOW_no-training_draft.docx (Markus attached earlier), subprocessors_list_202607.pdf, evidence_pack_instructions.pdf

Next steps I propose:
- We can adopt the short wording above into the DPA and add the operational appendix (evidence pack) as an exhibit.
- I'll assemble the evidence pack and aim to deliver the first set by end of week (Jul 16).
- Jordan: can you confirm the Dedicated BYOK timeline so I can include it in the SOW pricing note?

Elena — happy to hop on the call Monday at 10am CET if that still works.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@novamed.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 16:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: NovaMed: no-train commitment, SOW language, and KMS residency questions

David — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. The DPA insert looks good; Legal will suggest one very small edit to the prompt/output ownership line to call out "non-personal data outputs" explicitly (we'll send redline).

Please proceed with the evidence pack and subprocessors list. We can take the Dedicated BYOK path if you can confirm the 3–6 week timeline in writing and provide an estimated price delta for Dedicated during that period.

I'll share the DocuSign link for our standard DPA and loop in our Security lead on the call Monday.

Best regards,
Elena
